AI usage disclosure: I drafted every chapter myself, from what I learned building WSO2 MI Copilot , WSO2 BI Copilot and One Code . I used Claude Code and One Code to reorder each chapter so it leads with the answer (the Minto pyramid), to polish the English, to generate the diagrams, and to write the code that draws the charts.

A blog series about building AI agents from first principles, published as a book.

📖 Read it online: https://isuruwijesiri.com/harness-engineering-101/

An LLM API is stateless. Every turn, you send the entire conversation as a JSON array and get text back. A harness is the program that builds, maintains, and protects that array. Everything the field calls "agents" is a set of patches to that one loop, and each patch exists because something concrete broke. This series develops that one idea across 16 chapters, growing a ~300-line toy agent in plain Python as it goes.

I use the same ideas in One Code , an open-source coding agent built on pi .

The rendered book reads best online at the link above. If you'd rather read the source here on GitHub, follow the chapters in order below. The full introduction is on the book's landing page .

Every chapter has the same shape: the failure, the minimal patch, what the patch costs.

# Chapter The failure it patches 1 It's Just a JSON Array "How do I even talk to this thing?" 2 The Brain: A Next-Token Black Box "Why does it behave like that?" 3 Tools: JSON Mapped to Functions The brain can't touch the world 4 The Agent Loop One tool call isn't enough 5 Caching: Why Order Matters Resending the array gets expensive Part II — Running Long (the array under pressure) # Chapter The failure it patches 6 Context Is a Budget, Not a Bag The window fills up 7 Subagents: Fork the Context One array can't hold all the work 8 Steering the Running Loop The brain drifts mid-task 9 Background Work and Time The loop is synchronous; the world isn't Part III — The Ecosystem (naming what you already understand) # Chapter The failure it patches 10 Every Framework Is a Wrapper Around Chapter 1 Abstraction anxiety 11 Extending the Body: MCP, Skills, Deferred Loading, Hooks Capabilities don't fit in the array 12 Debugging the Array You can't fix the prompt you can't see Part IV — Trust, Domains, and Data # Chapter The failure it patches 13 Reflexes and Guardrails The loop will do something dumb 14 Case Study: Coding Agents How specialized does the body need to be? 15 RAG Was a Harness Pattern All Along A thousand names for one idea Epilogue Build Your Own : the complete toy harness, annotated Appendix — Advanced Topics Standalone pieces. Read them when you need them.

reactions: [Hacker News] Then point it to the Anthropic docs. Only place with reliable info. Look at their opus 5.5 prompting guide.
[Hacker News] this has been the exact analogy I've kept in my mind with LLMs

[Hacker News] It depends on the goal. Given powerful tools, Opus 5.5 will eventually get the job done, but it might have to write/test its own custom software to get there. If you're running the same task thousands of times that's you want to move that work into the harness (building the right tools, right instructions, right guidance). Once you move it into the harness, you probably no longer ne

[Hacker News] I think it would be fair to say the harness is the Kitchen and the model is the Chef. The Chef is very capable but limited to the tools, appliances, and ingredients in the Kitchen. If you say "make me a cake" but there's no oven and no flour, you're not going to get a very good cake.

[Hacker News] yep, plenty of other issues you didn't mention too. been working on refining the data pipelines. tbh I probably shouldn't have posted it at all, I just thought some might find it interesting. intended audience is people building harnesses (like myself) so that people can compare notes, implementation details, benchmarks, etc... thanks for the feedback

[Hacker News] That's totally fair at this point, and a bit expected. I'm still sprinting towards my definition of done for the core product surface. Hand-writing the docs (and a like, effective book) are some of the last things on the pre 1.0 list, too much churn until then.
